Four tests repeated the same setup. The edit and delete note command
tests already use a helper like this.

commitResults.messageTitle: Assert assumptions in note code
commitResults.messageBody:
The note code relied on these without checking them:

* setPersonKeepingIndex keeps the edited student in the filtered list.
* EditNoteCommand reads a note only after verifyNoteExists checks the
  NID.
* JsonAdaptedNote never gets null text, because JsonAdaptedPerson
  rejects null notes first.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject null arguments in note commands
commitResults.messageBody:
EditNoteCommand already rejects null arguments when it is created.
AddNoteCommand and DeleteNoteCommand did not, so a null would only
fail later, inside execute.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Explain why each filter can be given once
commitResults.messageBody:
filter rejects a repeated filter, but the DG justified this only for
t/. The tag aspect's argument doesn't carry over to every filter,
since a student can take several subjects.

Add an aspect comparing AND, OR, a mix of both, and allowing each
filter once, and point the tag aspect to it.

commitResults.messageTitle: UG: Remove the repeated filter tag bullet
commitResults.messageBody:

already says each filter, including t/, can be given only once. Its
t/paid example is about exact matching, so move it into the
exact-matching bullet and remove the tag bullet.
